path_literal_evidence.literal:
Pytest conftest for Cairn's bootstrap test suite.

Carries several mechanisms, all stdlib-only and all inert unless explicitly
activated: the **order-independence shuffle hook**, the **release-mode outcome
rule** and the **broad-run guard** (documented at
the section that implements it, near the end of this file).

Release mode (``CAIRN_RELEASE_GATE_ACTIVE``)
--------------------------------------------

``bootstrap/security_check.py`` sets this variable, at exactly one
recognized value, on the pytest children whose result it reports as
release evidence.  While it is set, an actual ``skipped`` /
``xfailed`` / ``xpassed`` outcome makes the session **non-zero**: "the
security gate may have skipped on the machine that cut the release" is
not acceptable release evidence, and a suite that exits 0 after a skip
says nothing about the code that did not run.

Three boundaries, each deliberate:

* **Without the token -- including at any other value -- contributor
  behaviour is unchanged.**  A local skip is a feature for someone
  without dev-deps installed; only a release run refuses it.
* It is an **outcome rule, not a marker census**.  An *inactive*
  ``skipif`` marker (condition false, test ran normally) does not fail
  a release for existing.  Counting markers would refuse a release for
  a skip that never happened.
* An **already-failing or interrupted session stays at its own exit
  code**.  Overwriting a ``2`` (interrupted) with a ``1`` would hide
  the more serious outcome behind the less serious one.

When pytest is invoked without ``--quality-gate-shuffle-seed``
(the normal case), the hook is a no-op and tests run in the
default collection order.  When the flag is passed, the hook
deterministically reorders ``items`` using a fresh ``random.Random``
seeded with the int value, so the same seed always produces the
same order.

Repeat-call protection: an invocation can pass multiple
``--quality-gate-shuffle-seed`` values; pytest keeps only the last
one.  That is sufficient for the quality-gate sub-gate's "run once
per seed" contract (the sub-gate spawns a subprocess per seed).

Refuse the session if any hook this module owns has been replaced.

    Checked from inside a hook rather than at module scope on purpose: module
    scope executes top-to-bottom, so a check placed in the file body runs
    *before* an append further down and sees the state it is meant to catch as
    still correct. A hook body runs after the import has completed, which is the
    only moment the final bindings are visible.

    Runs from ``pytest_addhooks``, which is call #1 for a conftest plugin --
    ahead of ``pytest_addoption``. An earlier version ran from ``addoption`` and
    claimed no earlier hook existed; that was false, and it left an append
    shadowing both hooks silent.

    **A known limit, stated rather than left to be rediscovered.** The
    comparison is by object identity (``globals().get(name) is not fn``), so
    it catches every *rebinding* of the module attribute -- a second ``def``,
    a ``functools.wraps`` wrap, a bare reassignment -- because all of those
    make ``globals()[name]`` a different object from the one ``_own`` recorded.
    It does **not** catch a mutation of that *same* object's internals:
    ``pytest_sessionfinish.__code__ = other.__code__`` leaves the name bound
    to the identical object ``_OWNED_HOOKS`` already holds, so the comparison
    finds nothing to report. Measured: this silences the release-mode outcome
    rule as completely as the pre-fix hazard -- exit 0, no ``RELEASE MODE``
    report, no diagnostic anywhere -- on a tree with a real skip present.  An
    explicit ``_OWNED_HOOKS.pop(name)`` ahead of a shadowing ``def`` reaches
    the same result by a different route (the shadow's own identity check
    then compares the registry against itself). Both require code written
    specifically to defeat this check; neither is the accidental shadowing --
    a future contributor copying this file's own ``def``/``@_own`` idiom --
    this guard was built to catch, and neither is closed here.

Register the security-family marker.

    Membership itself lives in ``bootstrap/tests/security_manifest.py``; this
    only makes the marker known so ``-m`` selections are not warnings.

security: a member of the security test family (see bootstrap/tests/security_manifest.py). Deselected from the per-change loop with -m 'not security'; always run by the release ceremony, which executes the entire suite with skips and xfails failing closed.

If set, shuffle test collection order deterministically using this integer as the seed.  Stdlib `random.Random`; no pytest plugin dependency.  Used by scripts/quality_gate.py --sub order-independence.

path_literal_evidence.literal:
The review and verification rules must reach the adopter, not only the doctrine.

`doctrine/` is **not installed into an adopter tree**, so a rule that lives
only there binds nobody who adopts Cairn. These rules therefore sit in
`templates/core/AGENTS.md`, the file every adopter receives and every agent
loads each session, and in Cairn's own root `AGENTS.md`, so that Cairn is bound
by the rules it ships.

The rules pinned here:

* **A review reads a commit, never a shared working tree.** In a working tree
  shared with an author, the reviewer's only write is its own review record;
  anything else that writes runs in a separate copy. A reverted, uncommitted
  file cannot be brought back with git, so this is the rule that prevents lost
  work.
* **A claim that a value reaches every member of a set is settled by
  mutation.** The missing member is a line that is not there, so reading a
  diff cannot see it. The ledger reports every mutant against an unmutated
  control, and an equivalence nobody measured counts as a survivor. Two
  clauses carry that meaning and are pinned for what they say, not only that
  they exist: the trigger is a claim about a set (not any defect), and an
  equivalent mutant is one a behaviour test *passes* under (a test that fails
  has killed it).
* **Boundary B governs a trivial change too.** Search for its owning tests
  and readers, then run those checks on the exact candidate bytes before
  commit, in an otherwise clean tree or separate copy. Its commit body records
  the mode, pending tree certification, search, commands, counts, interpreter,
  outcomes and omissions; the author owns the record and there is no Boundary
  C. A passing record may say `Implementation verified at <SHA>`; a known
  missing consumer, security check, or criterion keeps the work open. For
  planned work, Boundary B is `bounded` for mapped affected behavior and
  consumers, or `wide` for owning families, known integration and public paths,
  and standing gates when effects cannot be confidently bounded. Use `wide`
  for a contract or trust-ceremony surface. A full-tree certification is a
  separate authorized integration run and cannot close a missing change check.
* **"Substantive surface" is defined once.** It is anything that is not
  ordinary prose, and that includes prose a test or manifest pins. A narrower
  "code" reading misses exactly the template rewrite whose pinned prose broke
  tests its author never ran.
* **Code review is not External by default.** More distance on a review is
  the Maintainer's call on one named artifact, never a default and never
  something an agent applies. The usual procedure may be reworded, so this is
  pinned as an absence: the claim must not come back in either copy, in any
  capitalisation or line wrapping.

Each obligation is an alternation matched against whitespace-collapsed text, so
a rewording that keeps the obligation passes and a deletion fails. Node IDs are
the obligation labels, never the patterns, so rewording a pattern does not
rename (and so drop) a collected test.

Run from the Cairn repo root:
    python -m pytest bootstrap/tests/test_review_and_verification_rules_ship.py
. The doctrine holds the same rule, but adopters never receive doctrine/; removing it here removes it for them.

path_literal_evidence.literal:
Focused guards for the implementation verification boundaries.

These tests guard the prospective governing/template contract and the existing
quality-gate composition. They do not parse filled verification records or
select tests automatically; both are explicit v1 omissions.
There is no separate slow / networked tier
